styleContract.illustrationStyle: Simplified stickman/doodle explainer construction — circle heads, dot eyes, stick limbs, mitten hands — never a detailed or semi-realistic character
styleContract.lineLanguage: Uniform thin, clean black outlines of identical weight everywhere; no sketchiness, no variable line weight, no cross-hatching
styleContract.shapeLanguage: Simple geometric primitives — circles, rounded rectangles, straight or gently curved lines — never intricate or organic detail
styleContract.detailLevel: Minimal — enough to read instantly at a glance, never busy or cluttered
styleContract.shadingPolicy: None — flat solid fills only, no gradients, no soft shadow rendering, no highlights
styleContract.dimensionality: 2D flat, no 3D rendering, no depth shading, no perspective distortion beyond simple flat-layer staging
styleContract.realismLevel: Non-realistic, iconographic — identity is carried by a handful of discrete flat features, never facial realism
styleContract.backgroundStrategy: 2-3 flat color layers (background/midground/foreground), never a fully rendered or photographic environment
forbiddenStyleTraits: realistic anatomy, fingers, or necks on stickman characters
styleContract.colorStrategy: Use mostly two to three dark tones per scene to sell the blackout; reserve one accent color per frame (torch yellow, painted curb off-white, or khaki armband) to denote human presence or safety cues. Avoid more than one accent in a single close composition to keep clarity.
styleContract.lightingStrategy: Very low-key, 'pools of light' approach: scenes are dominated by darkness with small local light sources (torch cones, narrow window leaks, reflective paint). No global illumination; when a torch is in frame, render its cone as a solid flat wedge that only lights immediate foreground elements.

palette.environmentPaletteRules: Large planes (sky, buildings, streets) stay in primary dark hues; human figures use slightly lighter silhouette tones so they read against backgrounds. Accent/supporting colors are used sparingly and only for functional elements (curbs, torches, armbands, a single coat).
palette.contrastRules: High contrast between small warm accents (torch, painted curb) and dark backgrounds to guide viewer attention. Maintain low overall saturation; avoid bright neon or chrome-like colors.

world.architecture: Simplified mid-20th-century London terrace silhouettes: short rows of rectangular houses with simple pitched roofs, flat facades, and a few low lamp posts (which are unlit). Details kept minimal to suit the stickman style.
world.geography: Urban, dense row-house neighborhoods and broader, busier thoroughfares; scenes should imply an eight-million-person city through layered street rows and repeating building silhouettes rather than explicit skyline landmarks.
world.era: WWII-era London, late 1930s to 1940s; visual cues imply the period (blackout curtains, simple car/vehicle silhouettes) but avoid detailed, model-specific historical prop rendering.
world.recurringEnvironmentConstruction: 2-3 flat visual layers per scene: background building silhouettes, midground street and curb, foreground human figures or foreground detail (painted curb, torch light). Keep composition simple and readable in silhouette/flat color.
world.environmentalColorRules: Backgrounds and large surfaces use deep muted tones to imply darkness; small props and human accessories use a limited set of accent colors to guide focus (torch beam, painted curb, warden armband). No gradients or textures.
world.weatherTimeConventions: Dusk scenes: deep navy-blue sky band at top with a thin dusk strip when needed; night scenes: near-black skies. Time of night indicated by overall darkness level and presence/absence of a thin dusk band.
historicalScientificConstraints: No visible electric streetlights, neon signs, or lit windows when portraying enforced blackout conditions (unless the scene explicitly shows pre-blackout or a violation).
Blackout curtains should occlude most window light; small beams leaking are acceptable only when the script calls out an infraction.

objectLanguage.canonicalDescription: A heavy, opaque rectangle covering the full window area in flat deep charcoal (#262626), pinned edge-to-edge so no interior glow shows; when a breach is depicted, show a single narrow, vertical thin-offwhite sliver no wider than 1/12th of the window width.
objectLanguage.whyRecurring: The blackout curtain is the episode's primary visual shorthand for the enforced darkness and appears repeatedly in domestic interior and exterior shots.

objectLanguage.canonicalDescription: A narrow curb strip painted in flat off-white (#F2F2F2) along the edge of pavement; always shown as a single uninterrupted stripe following the pavement contour and sized so it reads clearly against the dark street.
objectLanguage.whyRecurring: Painted curbs are a recurring adaptation Londoners used to safely navigate in blackout conditions; they function as a visual motif for practical adaptation.

objectLanguage.canonicalDescription: A short handheld torch drawn as a small cylinder in muted dark gray with a short conical light wedge in very desaturated warm yellow (#D9C88A) limited to a narrow tight cone no wider than twice the holder's shoulder width; illuminate only immediate foreground, leaving surrounding space dark.
objectLanguage.whyRecurring: Torches (flashlights) are frequent props used to show human-scale visibility and the limited, localized light people relied on.

objectLanguage.canonicalDescription: A single flat band worn on the upper arm: muted khaki rectangle (#8D7B59) with a small white circle centered and a minimal black 'W' glyph; drawn proportionally so it is readable on a stickman arm at medium shots.
objectLanguage.whyRecurring: Air-raid wardens are a recurring institutional presence in blackout scenes; the armband identifies them quickly without creating a named recurring character.
